name: Burgan Bank
founded: 1975 (incorporated by Amiri Decree dated 27 Dec 1975 per FY2025 financial statements note 1; the annual report timeline gives 1977 as incorporation as a joint-stock company with the State of Kuwait as majority shareholder)
regulators: CMA Kuwait (custodian, investment advisory, portfolio management and unregistered securities brokerage licences)
ownership_summary: Listed on Boursa Kuwait and a subsidiary of Kuwait Projects Company Holding K.S.C.P. (KIPCO), itself Boursa-listed (FY2025 financial statements, note 1). The FY2025 annual report shows KIPCO (effective) 61%, PIFSS 8% and others 31%. A KD 50m rights issue (277.8m shares at 180 fils) closed on 14 Sep 2026, 133.57% subscribed, raising paid-up capital from KD 399.6m to KD 427.4m; KIPCO publicly committed to it on 12 Sep 2026, but its post-issue stake was not found.

shareholders.holder: Kuwait Projects Company Holding K.S.C.P. (KIPCO) - effective holding

government_link: Indirect - PIFSS (Kuwaiti state pension institution) held 8% per the FY2025 annual report; the controlling shareholder KIPCO is a listed private-sector holding company.
group_structure: Burgan Bank K.P.S.C. is the Kuwait parent of a regional banking group: Algeria Gulf Bank (86.01%), Tunis International Bank (86.70%), Burgan Bank A.S. Turkey (47.55%, consolidated), Burgan Bank Financial Services Ltd (DIFC, 100%) and United Gulf Bank B.S.C., Bahrain (100%, acquired in 2025 for USD 190m; shareholders approved renaming it Burgan Bank Bahrain on 3 Sep 2026, subject to MOIC/CBB approvals). Through UGB the group controls Kamco Investment Company K.S.C.P. (Kamco Invest; 63.01% effective interest at 31 Dec 2025, described in the annual report as UGB's 60% stake), which in turn owns First Securities Brokerage Co. (58.74% effective) and Kamco's DIFC, KSA, Jersey and Luxembourg entities. DOUBLE COUNTING: Kamco Invest is profiled separately as kw-kamco; its balance sheet is consolidated into Burgan's group totals, so do not add Kamco's total assets to Burgan's. Kamco's AUM (client assets) is off Burgan's balance sheet but is the group's main AUM figure, so do not count it twice when summing Burgan and Kamco wealth assets. Group figures also include Turkey, Algeria, Tunisia and Bahrain; Kuwait was 72% of total assets before consolidation adjustments in 2025.

footprint: FY2025 (annual report): 126 branches, 283 ATMs, 4.2k employees and 2.1mn customers group-wide. Kuwait: 132,853 customers, 29 branches, 1,109 employees, 156 ATMs. Algeria 66 branches, Turkey 28, Tunisia 3; UGB/Kamco in Bahrain, with the Kamco network also covering the UAE (DIFC), Saudi Arabia, UK and Jordan as shown on the annual report map.
customer_segments: Retail (mass and premium cards, consumer loans, Kanz prize-draw savings account), private banking and wealth management for HNW and UHNW clients, corporate banking, treasury and financial institutions; UGB (Bahrain) is being repositioned to wholesale banking for HNW individuals, family offices, corporates and financial institutions across Kuwait, Bahrain, UAE and Saudi Arabia.
business_lines: Kuwait segments: Corporate Banking; Retail Banking; Private and Wealth Management (tailored private banking, investment and advisory solutions for HNW clients, CMA-licensed custody, advisory, portfolio management and unregistered brokerage); Treasury, Financial Institutions and Investments. International: Burgan Bank Turkey (incl. ON digital bank, 1.5mn+ customers in four years), Algeria Gulf Bank, Tunis International Bank, United Gulf Bank. Asset management, investment banking and brokerage come through Kamco Invest (via UGB) and First Securities Brokerage.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Burgan's Kuwait Private Banking & Wealth Management unit (GM Meshari Abduljalil Ahmad/Shehab, since Oct 2023) serves HNW and UHNW clients with CMA licences for custody, investment advisory, portfolio management and unregistered securities brokerage, and offers local and international equities, fixed income and alternatives (real estate, private credit, private equity). The FY2025 annual report names building 'best-in-class private banking and wealth management' as a strategic pillar and reports PB loans +31%, deposits +37% and net income +35% (2025 vs 2023). Since acquiring United Gulf Bank in 2025, the bank uses group company Kamco Invest as its product factory: private-banking clients get Kamco funds, bonds, sukuk, structured products, private debt mandates and alternatives. PB is delivered through branches (Al-Shaheed, Al-Adailiya), a dedicated hotline and online banking. The Burgan app and internet banking pages do not mention investing. No bank-level AUM is disclosed. Burgan won Euromoney's 'Best for HNW in Kuwait' (Private Banking Awards 2026).

private_banking.detail: Private Banking & Wealth Management (Kuwait) for HNW/UHNW clients. Services: investment advisory by CMA-registered advisors, portfolio management, custody, unregistered securities brokerage and credit. Offered at Al-Shaheed and Al-Adailiya branches (second added Sep 2024), plus a PB hotline and online banking. Awards: MEED 2025 Best Client Service (Wealth & Private) and Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026 Best for HNW in Kuwait.

asset_management.detail: Through Kamco Invest (63.01% effective, held via UGB; profiled as kw-kamco). The bank itself holds a CMA portfolio management licence. No bank-level fund range found.

brokerage.detail: Bank holds a CMA unregistered securities brokerage licence (S9). Group brokerage: First Securities Brokerage Company (58.74% effective, via Kamco) in Kuwait, and Burgan Yatirim Menkul Degerler A.S. in Turkey (S4 note). No retail online brokerage channel found at the bank.

digital_investing.detail: The Burgan App, Internet Banking, SMS, phone and WhatsApp channels are described without any investment features (S10). The only investing reference is a 'Daily Investment' deposit account. A 2025 Investor Relations app serves shareholders, not clients.

advisory.detail: Investment advisory licence; investment advisors registered with Kuwait CMA (S9). The annual report describes a 'personalised, client-centric advisory platform' (S4 p.22).

discretionary.detail: Holds a CMA Portfolio Management licence and offers 'portfolio services' (S9, S4), but discretionary mandates are not described explicitly.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model portfolio or robo-advice offering found on the wealth page, digital page or annual report.

funds_platform.detail: Private clients get access to Kamco funds, bonds and sukuk (+9.7x clients invested in Kamco funds YoY per annual report). A 2024 article mentions selected funds, bonds and equities, with regional and international options (Dubai, London, KSA). No third-party fund platform provider named.

structured_products.detail: Annual report: the Kamco partnership 'enables client participation in alternative investments, bonds, sukuk, and structured products' (PDF p.23).

private_markets.detail: Wealth page lists alternative investments (real estate, private credit, private equity). The annual report cites private debt mandates (+4.7x YoY) and VC/fund initiatives with Kamco.

islamic_wealth.detail: Sukuk access via Kamco is mentioned (S4). No dedicated Shariah-compliant wealth proposition was found. UGB (to become Burgan Bank Bahrain) will emphasise Islamic financing in wholesale banking (S6).

partners.what: Supplies funds, bonds, sukuk, structured products, alternatives and private debt mandates to Burgan private-banking clients; co-hosts an annual investment conference

initiatives.what: Extended private banking services to the Al-Adailiya branch (second PB branch after Al-Shaheed); CMA licences for custody, advisory, portfolio management and brokerage
Completed acquisition of 100% of United Gulf Bank (USD 190m), bringing UGB's ~60% stake in Kamco Invest into the group; PB/Kamco synergy programme
Strategy pillars: double retail market share; build best-in-class private banking and wealth management; promote digital offerings for new segments
Q1 2026: Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026 'Best for HNW in Kuwait'; preparing to relaunch the Kanz account
UGB shareholders approved renaming UGB to Burgan Bank Bahrain, focused on wholesale banking for HNW individuals, family offices, corporates and FIs (pending MOIC/CBB approvals)
KD 50m rights issue closed, 133.57% subscribed; Kamco Invest acted as issuance advisor and subscription agent

opportunities: Building 'best-in-class private banking and wealth management' is a named strategic pillar, alongside 'promote digital offerings for new segments' (FY2025 annual report, S4 p.21).

Burgan's client channels for wealth are branches, a hotline and online banking. The Burgan App and digital banking pages show no investing features (S10, S12), so there is no evident self-directed or digital wealth channel.
PB serves HNW/UHNW clients with local and international equities, fixed income and alternatives, using a CMA portfolio-management licence (S9).
barriers: The in-group product factory Kamco Invest already supplies funds, bonds, sukuk, structured products and private-market access to Burgan PB clients (S4 p.23), which reduces the need for a third-party product shelf.
Profit pressure: H1 2026 net profit fell 47% to KWD 11.1m, partly because of higher operating expenses from digital investment (S3, S5).
Controlled by KIPCO, and group wealth capability sits in Kamco (via UGB), so decisions may be taken at group or Kamco level (S4).
